programs.name: Managed Long Term Care (personal care / home care through an MLTC plan)

programs.name: Supplemental Security Income with NY State Supplement

programs.keyRule: 2026 SSI + NY supplement, individual living alone: $1,081/mo ($994 + $87); SSI resource limit $2,000.

programs.name: Medicare Savings Program - Qualified Medicare Beneficiary
programs.reason: Income $1,050 is under the QMB limit; pays Part B premium and Medicare cost-sharing; may already be active with her Medicaid.

programs.name: Medicare Part D Extra Help

programs.name: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program

programs.name: Home Energy Assistance Program

programs.name: VA Pension / Aid and Attendance

families.notes: NY 2026 Medicaid dollar limits come from NY Health Access (legal services, secondary) citing GIS 26 MA/03; MSP limits confirmed on health.ny.gov. EPIC-Medicaid exclusion stated from general knowledge, not a fetched page. If she needs 24-hour supervision because of wandering, MLTC plans often resist split-shift/24-hour care; may need advocacy. Consider SSI: may already be receiving it.

programs.name: Veterans Pension with Aid and Attendance
programs.reason: Served 1962-1965 including days after 5 Aug 1964 (Vietnam era), over 90 days, honorable, 65+. Net worth ~$75,000 incl. income is under $163,699. $37,200 income minus medical costs above $1,141 (two Part B premiums ~$4,870/yr) is about $33,470, under the $34,488 cap; paid home care raises the benefit. programs.name: VA Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers

programs.keyRule: 2026 NY QI: at or below $3,375/mo couple (186% FPL + $20); no resource test.

programs.name: Medicare Part D Extra Help

programs.name: Elderly Pharmaceutical Insurance Coverage

families.notes: QI is a striking NY-specific win: in most states this couple would be over the MSP limit. VA pension estimate assumes they pay both Part B premiums themselves; once QI pays those premiums, that deduction disappears, so the VA pension then depends on other medical costs (e.g. paid home care). Sequence matters: a counselor would document paid-care costs. HEAP and SNAP 2025-26 figures are from secondary sources. SCRIE $75,000 limit (eff. 1 Jul 2026) from secondary source.

families.notes: NY has an 'immediate need' fast-track for personal care/CDPAP for applicants not yet on Medicaid; not verified from a primary page here.
